title: Tech Mahindra and Infinite Uptime Partner to Scale Physical AI in Manufacturing
excerpt: The deal pairs Infinite Uptime's PlantOS™ prescriptive-intelligence platform with Tech Mahindra's global IT-OT transformation capabilities, targeting steel, cement, chemicals, and mining — first in North America and Europe.
body:
• Tech Mahindra (NSE: TECHM) and industrial-AI startup Infinite Uptime announced a partnership to scale Physical AI — AI applied to machines and plant processes — across manufacturing and process industries.
  • The deal pairs Infinite Uptime's PlantOS™, a physics-aware prescriptive-intelligence platform, with Tech Mahindra's end-to-end IT-OT transformation capabilities and global reach.
  • Tech Mahindra will apply its SIIM methodology — Simulate, Integrate, Implement, Maintain — to validate and deploy the solutions inside existing production environments.
  • The joint go-to-market will target asset-intensive sectors such as steel, cement, chemicals, metals and mining, with an initial focus on North America and Europe.

Tech Mahindra and Pune-based industrial-AI startup Infinite Uptime have announced a partnership to accelerate the adoption of Physical AI across manufacturing and process industries, combining the startup's PlantOS™ platform with the IT major's global systems-integration muscle.

The partnership, announced this week out of Atlanta and Pune, pairs PlantOS™ — Infinite Uptime's Industrial Outcome Intelligence Engine, which delivers physics- and vertical-aware prescriptive intelligence for industrial reliability — with Tech Mahindra's global reach, industry relationships, and end-to-end IT-OT transformation capabilities. The two will take the combined offering to market under a proposition spanning Physical AI and Industrial Outcome Intelligence.

Context & Background

The pitch addresses a frustration manufacturers know well. Plants have spent years investing in sensors, connectivity, analytics, and AI to detect equipment and production problems. Detection alone, however, does not improve performance — the harder job is understanding the physical context, deciding the right response, getting frontline workers to act on it, and verifying the result.

PlantOS™ is designed to close that loop by combining mechanical and process signals with physics-aware contextualisation and failure-mode intelligence. It gives operators specific recommendations — what action to take, why it is required, and when to complete it — and lets them validate the impact on plant performance. Infinite Uptime says its 99% Trust Loop ensures high-accuracy AI prescriptions are acted upon and the results confirmed by operators. Across its deployments, the company reports more than 167,837 hours of operator-validated downtime savings across over 1,000 plants, 172 customers, nine industrial verticals, and 28 countries.

Tech Mahindra will apply its SIIM methodology — Simulate, Integrate, Implement, and Maintain — to validate, integrate, and deploy Physical AI solutions across existing production, operational-technology, and enterprise environments, embedding the prescriptive intelligence inside complex plant operations rather than layering it on top.

"The next phase of industrial transformation will be shaped by the ability to convert industrial intelligence into timely action."

— Manikantan NS, SVP & Global Head of Manufacturing Vertical, Tech Mahindra

Impact & Analysis

The partnership will target asset-intensive sectors — steel, cement, chemicals, metals and mining, pulp and paper — and while the go-to-market is global, the initial focus will be North America and Europe, particularly larger transformation programmes where equipment reliability and production performance are closely connected.

For Infinite Uptime, the deal plugs a deep-tech product into a sales and delivery engine: Tech Mahindra employs more than 146,000 professionals across 90 countries and brings decades of enterprise-integration experience. For Tech Mahindra, part of the Mahindra Group, PlantOS™ adds a specialised industrial-intelligence layer it can embed into broader operational-technology modernisation programmes.

The partnership also lands amid growing interest in Physical AI — AI applied to machines and industrial processes rather than operating purely in digital environments. Infinite Uptime was recognised by Gartner in the 2026 Magic Quadrant for Global Industrial AIoT Platforms. Founded in 2015 by Raunak Bhinge, the startup has raised roughly $65 million — including a $35 million Series C led by Avataar Ventures in March 2025 and an earlier round led by Tiger Global — and counts Vedanta, JSW, and Tata Group among its customers.

"Physical AI creates lasting value when it gives frontline teams the context and confidence to take the right action and verify the result."

— Karthikeyan Natarajan, CEO, Infinite Uptime

Diaspora Angle

This is a story with a natural home in the diaspora narrative: a Pune deep-tech startup, backed by global investors and led by Indian founders, scaling worldwide on the shoulders of one of India's best-known IT services exporters. For the many Indian engineers and managers working in manufacturing and plant operations across North America and Europe — the partnership's initial focus markets — the combined offering could soon show up in their own facilities. It also illustrates how Indian IT is climbing the value chain, from body-shopping and software services to specialised AI products deployed on factory floors.

What's Next

The real test of the partnership will be commercial: converting the joint proposition into signed transformation programmes with large industrial customers, starting in North America and Europe. Watch for customer announcements and case studies with measured downtime or productivity figures — in industrial AI, validated outcomes on the plant floor, not pilot press releases, are what move the market.
